encounters.cc: Persistent urinary issues with difficulty initiating stream, slow interrupted flow, and sensation of incomplete emptying worsening over the past year.

lines: Persistent urinary issues with difficulty initiating stream, slow interrupted flow, and sensation of incomplete emptying worsening over the past year.

This 71-year-old male with Parkinson's disease and associated autonomic dysfunction, including orthostatic hypotension and chronic constipation, returns for follow-up of persistent urinary dysfunction.
He reports that over the past year, he often feels the need to urinate but has difficulty initiating the stream.
When able to void, the urine flow is slow and intermittently interrupted, and he frequently feels he has not fully emptied his bladder.
Over the last several months, he has begun noticing dampness in his underwear and occasional episodes of urine leakage, especially at night, though he is often unaware of when the leakage occurs.
He denies burning with urination, blood in the urine, or urgency.
He has also had episodes of numbness and tingling in his feet and recently began using a cane due to unsteadiness while walking.
- Neurogenic bladder secondary to sacral nerve root injury
His past medical history is significant for hypertension and long-standing poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus.

encounters.cc: Persistent bradykinesia, mild tremor at rest, and rigidity despite optimized levodopa therapy; interested in clinical trial enrollment.

lines: Persistent bradykinesia, mild tremor at rest, and rigidity despite optimized levodopa therapy; interested in clinical trial enrollment.
The patient is a 72-year-old male with Parkinson's disease and autonomic dysfunction who returns for follow-up of motor symptoms.
Previously evaluated for orthostatic hypotension and neurogenic bladder, he is now enrolled in a clinical trial evaluating cognitive and motor effects of novel adjunct therapy.
Despite optimized levodopa/carbidopa and dopamine agonist treatment, he reports persistent bradykinesia, mild tremor at rest, and rigidity.
He also describes orthostatic lightheadedness and daytime fatigue.
After 4 weeks of therapy, he reports increased energy, improved concentration, and better mobility.
